modules.title: Client & Domain
modules.summary: Business context, terminology, stakeholders and project objectives for Project ADB.
modules.description: Establish the shared vocabulary of the programme so that every conversation with the client, the product owner and the delivery team starts from the same understanding of the domain.
objectives: Describe the business problem Project ADB addresses
Explain the core banking domain vocabulary used daily
Identify the key stakeholders and their decision rights
State the three measurable objectives agreed with the client
keyTakeaways: ADB replaces four legacy servicing systems with a single core platform
Account origination is the highest-value journey in phase one
Every change request is assessed against the three agreed objectives

blocks.text: Project ADB modernises the account origination and servicing journey for Meridian Financial Services. Today the journey spans four legacy systems, three reconciliation spreadsheets and a manual document control process. Average onboarding time for a new SME customer is 9 days, against a target of 2.

items: Consolidate origination, KYC and servicing into one platform
Remove the nightly reconciliation batch between core systems
Give relationship managers a single view of customer status
Make onboarding auditable end to end

blocks.title: Programme in one line
blocks.text: Ship the ADB core platform, prove it with Meridian's pilot branch cohort, and prepare for the phase-two migration of servicing.

rows: The journey that creates a new customer record and product holding
The evidence bundle that satisfies the client's due-diligence policy
A post-sale change to an existing customer, such as an address update
The relationship owner who initiates most origination journeys
The daily boundary after which changes settle the next working day

blocks.text: These five terms cover roughly 80% of the vocabulary used in the daily scrum. If a term is not in this list, ask your product analyst before making an assumption about it.
The ADB platform replaces four legacy servicing systems with a single core platform, and cuts new-customer onboarding from nine days to two.
blocks.author: Programme objectives, agreed with Meridian Financial Services

blocks.text: Three stakeholder groups shape day-to-day decisions. The client product owner prioritises the backlog, the Meridian delivery lead approves environment and data decisions, and the HCLTech engineering lead owns technical standards and quality gates.

items: Client product owner — owns scope and acceptance
Meridian delivery lead — owns data, access and environment readiness
HCLTech engineering lead — owns standards, releases and quality gates
Learning program manager — owns induction and readiness for every new joiner

blocks.title: Escalation path
blocks.text: Domain questions that block delivery escalate to the product analyst first. Raise them in the shared channel rather than waiting for the weekly sync — the sync is for decisions, not for unblocking yourself.

modules.title: Environment & Access
modules.summary: Required tools, the access-request process, approved setup guidance and common setup issues.
modules.description: Everything needed to get a productive workstation running on day one, including how to request the access you do not yet have.
objectives: Request the access bundle for your learning role
Complete the approved workstation setup checklist
Diagnose the four most common access and setup failures
Locate the support channels for blocked access requests
keyTakeaways: Access is granted by role bundle, not by individual request
The Dev baseline takes 90 minutes on a clean corporate laptop
A failed MFA enrolment is resolved by IT within one working day

blocks.text: Access is provisioned as a bundle matched to your learning role. The platform, the source control, the CI pipeline and the environment are granted together so that your first commit does not fail on a missing permission.

rows: Repository, IDE, CI, development and integration environments
Test management, Jira, browser lab, reporting access
All baseline access plus production read-only and reporting

blocks.title: Requesting access
blocks.text: Raise the access request through the service desk using the template named after your learning role. Your manager approves the business justification; IT fulfils it.

items: Join the HCLTech domain and complete multi-factor enrolment
Install the pinned engineering baseline from the software portal
Clone the repository from the organisation path, not a personal fork
Verify the toolchain with the standard environment check script
Complete one successful build on the development environment

blocks.code:
# Verify the pinned toolchain before your first commit
hcl env verify --profile developer

# Expected output
[ok] node      20.15.0   (pinned 20.15.x)
[ok] jdk       17.0.9    (pinned 17.x)
[ok] database  client    16.x
[warn] container runtime not detected - optional

blocks.text: The verification script is safe to run at any time. If a line reports a mismatch, do not attempt to upgrade the tool locally — use the pinned installer so that your environment matches the build agents.

items: Certificate trust error on the internal registry — re-import the corporate root certificate and restart the terminal
Repository permission denied on the first clone — request the role bundle, not repository-level access
MFA device already registered — remove the old enrolment before adding a new device
VPN splits the internal registry route — connect before the installer runs

blocks.title: Never share credentials
blocks.text: Access is individual and audited. Sharing a token, a password or a session cookie breaches the project information handling policy and will result in access removal.

modules.title: Application Overview
modules.summary: Application purpose, key functional areas, user journeys and the high-level business flow.
modules.description: A guided tour of the ADB platform: the bounded contexts it is built from, the journey an account manager drives, and where the interesting logic lives.
objectives: Describe the purpose and bounded contexts of the ADB platform
Trace the happy path of a customer origination journey
Identify which functional area owns a given business rule
Explain how the platform integrates with the client estate
keyTakeaways: The platform is organised into five bounded contexts with explicit ownership
Origination is a saga: each step can be compensated independently
Nothing writes to the core ledger directly — all movement flows through the posting service

blocks.text: The ADB platform provides origination, servicing and reporting for Meridian's retail and SME customer base. It is deliberately split into five bounded contexts so that each has one owning team and one clear contract.

blocks.title: Why the split matters
blocks.text: Business rules belong to exactly one context. If a change appears to affect two, it usually means the rule is in the wrong place — raise it in design review rather than duplicating the logic.

items: Capture the customer intent and validate mandatory details
Run the KYC pack assembly and the client screening checks
Select products and apply the pricing rules
Execute the client-side verification handshake
Open the accounts and post the opening balances
Emit the confirmation pack and close the case

blocks.text: Each step is a separate, resumable operation. If the client screening check fails, the journey pauses and returns a structured reason code rather than failing silently — this is what makes the saga compensable.

items: Client CRM supplies customer intent and relationship ownership
The core banking host remains the system of record for balances
The screening service handles sanctions and PEP checks synchronously
Document generation produces the customer-facing pack asynchronously

blocks.text: Nothing writes to the core ledger directly — all movement flows through the posting service, which is the only component that holds ledger credentials.
blocks.author: Architecture decision record ADR-014

modules.title: Security & Guidelines
modules.summary: Access procedures, information handling, project restrictions and compliance expectations.
modules.description: The rules that keep client data safe, and the reasoning behind them. Read this module carefully — it is assessed and it is enforced.
objectives: Handle client data according to the classification policy
Apply the project restrictions that apply to your role
Recognise and report a security incident promptly
Meet the compliance expectations attached to this engagement
keyTakeaways: Client data never leaves approved environments, including your own laptop
Production data is masked in every non-production environment
Suspected incidents are reported within one hour, without investigating first

rows: Customer identity documents, credentials, live balances
Approved environment only, no local copy
Encrypted at rest, shared on a need-to-know basis
Team schedules, sprint plans, process documents
Company systems and approved collaboration tools

blocks.title: No client data on personal devices
blocks.text: Downloading client data to a personal device, a personal cloud drive or a personal AI assistant is prohibited, regardless of the volume.

items: Production change freeze runs from the last business day of each month
Direct database access in production is prohibited; use the approved servicing tools
Client-side code may not be published to any public repository
Third-party tools require a security review before use with project data

blocks.text: These restrictions are not negotiable and are audited by the client's assurance team on a monthly basis. If a task appears to require breaking one, stop and raise it — the correct answer is never to proceed quietly.

items: Stop the activity and secure the data you are working with
Report through the security helpline within one hour of discovery
Preserve the state — do not delete logs, files or messages
Wait for direction from the security team before communicating further

blocks.title: Do not self-investigate
blocks.text: You are not expected to determine the scope or the cause. Reporting quickly is what limits impact, and you will never be penalised for a good-faith report.

modules.title: Development Lifecycle & Standards
modules.summary: Requirement understanding, task workflow, branching, pull requests, reviews and logging.
modules.description: How work moves from a requirement to a released change on ADB, and the conventions the team expects you to follow.
objectives: Interpret a requirement before writing any code
Follow the agreed branch and pull request conventions
Write a reviewable pull request that passes the review checklist
Log work to the standard expected by the delivery lead
keyTakeaways: Branches are named feature/<ticket>-<slug> and are rebased, never merged
Every pull request needs one reviewer and one linked ticket
Daily logging is mandatory — it is the client-mandated audit trail

blocks.text: A ticket is a starting point, not a specification. Before writing code, restate the requirement in your own words, list the acceptance criteria you can verify, and flag the assumptions you are making. A five-minute clarification now prevents a day of rework later.

items: Read the ticket and the linked acceptance criteria
Check the domain glossary for the business vocabulary
Write down your assumptions and share them with the product analyst
Break the work into a slice you can deliver in one day

blocks.title: Ask in the channel, not in a meeting
blocks.text: Domain questions belong in the shared project channel so that the answer is searchable and reusable by the next joiner.

items: Branch from develop using feature/<ticket>-<slug>
Rebase onto the latest develop rather than merging develop into your branch
Keep pull requests under 400 changed lines
One ticket per pull request, one reviewer minimum
Squash merge only after the pipeline is green

blocks.code:
git switch develop
git pull --rebase
git switch -c feature/ADB-1421-case-retry

# ... commit your work ...

git fetch origin
git rebase origin/develop
git push --force-with-lease

blocks.text: Force-push to your own feature branch is expected and safe. Never force-push to develop, release or any shared branch.

rows: Does the change satisfy every acceptance criterion?
Is the new behaviour covered by an automated test?
Is client data handled according to the classification policy?
Is there enough logging to diagnose a production issue?

blocks.text: Daily logging is mandatory — it is the client-mandated audit trail.
blocks.author: ADB delivery guidelines, section 4

modules.title: Unit Testing & Release Awareness
modules.summary: Unit testing, debugging, defect-fix verification, quality gates and release responsibilities.
modules.description: What quality means on this project: the tests you own, the gates your change must pass, and how a release is put together.
objectives: Write unit tests that assert behaviour rather than implementation
Use the debugging workflow the team relies on
Verify a defect fix with a regression test that would have caught it
Describe the release quality gates and your responsibilities in them
keyTakeaways: A test that cannot fail is not a test — mutation-check your assumptions
Every defect fix ships with a test that reproduces the original failure
The release gate requires green pipeline, reviewer approval and an updated changelog

blocks.text: The team follows test-driven development for domain logic. A test describes an observable behaviour of the unit, using the public interface only, so that a refactor does not break the suite.

items: Arrange, act, assert — one behaviour per test
No network calls, no sleeps, no reliance on test execution order
Assert on the business outcome, not on log output or internal fields
Every domain rule needs at least one boundary case
Reproduce the failure locally with the smallest possible input
Write a failing test that captures the failure
Find the cause — a failing test narrows the search considerably
Fix the cause, not the symptom
Run the full module suite before you push

blocks.title: Never fix it in production
blocks.text: A hotfix that is not covered by a regression test will be re-broken by the next release. If a hotfix is genuinely unavoidable, the test is raised as a follow-up ticket before the change is closed.
A release is cut from the release branch, never from a feature branch. The release manager coordinates the cut; every developer owns the changelog entry for their own change.

modules.title: Testing Strategy & Design
modules.summary: Testing lifecycle, test types, environments, acceptance criteria and exception scenarios.
modules.description: The testing approach for ADB: the levels of test, the pyramid the team maintains, and how a test case is designed so that it is useful.
objectives: Describe the test levels and the shape of the test pyramid
Select the right environment for a given test activity
Derive executable test cases from acceptance criteria
Design explicit tests for exception and negative scenarios
keyTakeaways: Most defects are found at unit level, so the pyramid is deliberately wide at the base
Acceptance criteria are the source of truth for test design
An exception path without a test is an uncovered risk, not a low priority

items: Unit — domain rules and edge cases, owned by the developer
Component — a bounded context exercised in isolation
Contract — the agreement between two contexts
Integration — the journey across contexts and external systems
System — the end-to-end journey the client cares about

blocks.text: The team's target ratio is roughly 70% unit, 20% integration and 10% end-to-end. A suite that inverts this ratio is slow, flaky and expensive, and it will not sustain a two-week release cadence.

blocks.title: Your role on the pyramid
blocks.text: As a tester you author the component, contract and system level suites. You do not write unit tests for domain code, but you do raise defects when the unit behaviour contradicts the acceptance criteria.
Client data is masked in every non-production environment. If a test needs a specific data shape, it is created from the approved synthetic data generator rather than copied from production.

items: Read the acceptance criterion and identify the observable outcome
Define the preconditions and the seeded data
Write the happy path first
Derive the boundary and negative cases
Define the expected result precisely enough to be automated

blocks.code:
AC-3  When screening returns a manual-review outcome,
     the case pauses with reason code KYC_MANUAL_REVIEW
     and remains resumable.

TC-114  Given a case in 'kyc-screening' with a manual-review
     screening outcome, when the screening step executes, then the
     case status is 'paused', the reason code is 'KYC_MANUAL_REVIEW'
     and the case is resumable.

blocks.title: Negative cases are not optional
blocks.text: Every exception path in the requirements needs an explicit negative case. If it is not specified, raise it with the product analyst — an unspecified exception is a design gap, not a testing inconvenience.

modules.title: Test Data & Execution
modules.summary: Approved test-data practices, test execution, evidence capture, result reporting and retesting.
modules.description: How test data is created, how a suite is executed and traced, and how the evidence trail is produced for the client.
objectives: Create compliant test data through the approved generator
Execute a suite and record the outcome in the tracker
Capture evidence that satisfies the client audit requirement
Retest a defect fix and close it correctly
keyTakeaways: All test data is synthetic and generated, never copied from production
A defect cannot be closed without an attached execution evidence link
Retesting happens on the same environment and the same data as the original failure

items: Generate data with the approved synthetic data generator
Never copy, export or screenshot production customer records
Seed identifiers deterministically so that failures are reproducible
Clean up seeded data at the end of each execution window

blocks.code:
# Create a deterministic seed for a test execution
hcl testdata seed --profile sme-retail --count 50 --seed 20260412

# Verify the environment is clean before execution
hcl testdata verify --environment system-test

blocks.title: Real identities are never used
blocks.text: Even when a defect requires a specific value, reproduce it with synthetic data that has the same shape. The client audits test-data provenance quarterly.

items: Confirm the environment and the data seed before starting
Execute the suite in the tracker, one test case at a time
Attach the evidence artefact — screenshot, log excerpt or API trace
Update the result status and add a note explaining anything unusual
Summarise the run and publish it to the shared channel

rows: Observed behaviour matches the expected result
Observed behaviour deviates from the expected result
Raise an environment defect, do not mark as failed
The case is not applicable in this cycle

blocks.text: A fix is retested on the same environment and the same data as the original failure. Retesting on a different environment frequently produces a false pass and sends a real defect back into the release.

blocks.title: Closing a defect
blocks.text: A defect is closed only when the retest passes and the evidence link is present. If the fix is incomplete, reopen the defect with a note rather than raising a new one.

modules.title: Defect, Regression & Release Validation
modules.summary: Defect reporting, severity and priority, regression selection, smoke testing and release-readiness checks.
modules.description: How defects are raised and prioritised, how the regression suite is selected for a release, and what a release readiness review checks.
objectives: Write a defect report that a developer can act on immediately
Distinguish severity from priority and apply the project's definitions
Select a regression scope appropriate to the change
Run a smoke suite and reach a defensible release recommendation
keyTakeaways: Severity describes the impact; priority describes the urgency — they are not the same
Regression scope is risk-based, and the selection is documented
A release recommendation always states what was and was not tested

rows: The system is unusable or data is at risk
Posting service cannot reach the core ledger
A core journey is broken with no workaround
A new customer cannot be onboarded at all
A journey is broken but a workaround exists
Statement totals are wrong for one account type
A label is truncated on a narrow screen

blocks.text: Priority is separate from severity. A Minor cosmetic issue on a customer-facing journey can be higher priority than a Major issue in an internal tool. Priority reflects urgency, severity reflects impact.

blocks.title: A good defect report
blocks.text: Include what you expected, what happened, the environment and data seed, and the evidence. A report that needs a question to understand is a report that will sit in the queue.

items: Always include the smoke suite and the impacted journey
Add every suite that shares a service or data with the change
Include the last three release regression suites as a baseline
Document the selection and the rationale in the release ticket

blocks.text: Regression selection is risk-based, not habit-based. Selecting the full suite every cycle is not safer — it is slower, and a suite that always runs eventually gets skipped under pressure.

items: Run the smoke suite on the release candidate
Confirm the regression scope completed with no new failures
Verify the defect backlog for anything blocking release
Publish the release recommendation with an explicit list of what was not tested

blocks.text: A release recommendation always states what was and was not tested — an unqualified 'ready' is not an acceptable answer.
blocks.author: ADB release readiness checklist
